title: Police cleared in man's death: SIU rules collision with suspect `unavoidable'
article: SIU director Peter Tinsley concluded the police van was moving slowly and "the collision was unavoidable as a result of the unexpected movement of Mr. \[Benoit Aube\]'s bicycle into the path of the police vehicle."
Ontario's Special Investigations Unit has cleared an Ottawa police officer in the death of a man on a bicycle killed by a police van while officers chased suspects in an attempted break-in.
On June 22, several officers, including a tactical unit van, responded to a theft in progress in the Byward Market area, and the van began chasing the suspects.
The van hit Benoit Aube, 38, on Clarence Street near Cumberland Street, and he was pinned under one of the vehicle's front wheels for about 30 minutes.
He suffered a head injury and died two days later at the Ottawa Hospital's General campus.

The SIU, a civilian agency that investigates circumstances involving police and civilians that result in serious injury or death, concluded there are no grounds to believe the officer committed a criminal offence during the chase.
Six SIU investigators interviewed the driver and nine other witnesses, and reviewed police notes and tapes.

SIU director Peter Tinsley concluded the police van was moving slowly and "the collision was unavoidable as a result of the unexpected movement of Mr. Aube's bicycle into the path of the police vehicle."
